_comment: Activity feedback questions, from the APP_Questions document ops supplied and
TWO DIFFERENT SYSTEMS — do not conflate them, the field names differ:
question: { answers[], description, id, is_peer, questionText, type:'scq' }
whose first question is exactly the STUDENTS/Prep [AWARENESS] entry below.
surveys/{id}  — TEACHER questions, one per activity (activities/{id} shares the
SAME doc id and carries the stage).
NOT fully templatable: summaryMap text is written per ACTIVITY, not per stage,
so it cannot be generated from this document. The teacher wording is recorded
COVERAGE GAPS in the source document — no questions exist for:
students: foundation, secondary   peers: foundation, secondary   teacher: secondary
'Middle' as a stage prefix is inferred; only 'Prep-' is confirmed from live data.

student.description: Think about if you were paying attention and understood what to do and tried to finish the activity nicely.
student.questionText: Did I listen carefully when my teacher was giving instructions?

student.description: Think if you tried something in your own way or came up with a fun or new idea during the activity, or did something in a way that was a little different or special from others.
student.questionText: Did I try something new or use my own idea in the activity?

student.description: Think about how it felt to do the activity with your classmates and friends, did you share, help, or enjoy being in a group?
student.questionText: Did I like working with my classmates?

student.description: Would you like to do this activity one more time?
student.questionText: Would I like to do this activity again?

student.description: Think about whether you tried to get help from your teacher or friends when you were confused.
student.questionText: Did I ask for help when I did not understand something?

peer.description: Think about if your friend paid attention to the teacher and tried to do the activity carefully.
peer.questionText: Did this friend listen to the teacher carefully and follow the instructions?

peer.description: Think about if your friend helped others and worked happily with classmates.
peer.questionText: Was this friend kind and spoke nicely to other classmates?

peer.description: Think if your friend said something new, fun, or helpful that others didn’t think of, or said something that made it easier for others to do the activity.
peer.questionText: Did this friend share any new or interesting ideas during the activity?

student.description: Think if you were able to listen carefully to your teacher’s instructions, stay on task, and not get distracted too much during the activity.
student.questionText: Was I able to stay focused and follow what my teacher was asking me to do?

student.description: Think if something you learnt during this activity can help you outside school, like at home, in the playground, in your neighbourhood, or with friends.
student.questionText: Did this activity teach me something that I can use in my real life?

student.description: Think about how much effort you put into your work. Did you complete it carefully? In the end, did it make you feel good about what you have done?
student.questionText: Did I try my best in this activity and feel proud of what I did?

student.description: Think about whether you gave your own idea, used your imagination, or did something in a way that was different from others. Did you try a new way to finish the task or add your own special touch to it?
student.questionText: Did I try to think in a different way, try something new in my own style, or have any unique idea during the activity?

student.description: Think about whether you noticed how you were feeling while doing the activity, like feeling happy, confused, or excited.
student.questionText: Was I able to understand how I was feeling during the activity and express or share my emotions clearly?

peer.description: Think about if your friend paid attention to the teacher and tried to do the activity carefully.
peer.questionText: Did this friend listen to the teacher carefully and follow the instructions?

peer.description: Think about if your friend helped others and worked happily with classmates.
peer.questionText: Was this friend kind and spoke nicely to other classmates?

peer.description: Think if your friend said something new, fun, or helpful that others didn’t think of, or said something that made it easier for others to do the activity.
peer.questionText: Did this friend share any new or interesting ideas during the activity?

questions.questionText: To what extent did the learner stay attentive and follow instructions during the activity?
To what extent did the learner express their emotions clearly and respond with care towards people or situations?
To what extent did the learner attempt to share original thoughts, try new approaches, or express ideas in a unique way?
